questions.stem: Why do the carbon anodes need to be replaced regularly during the extraction of aluminium?

options.text: The oxygen produced at the anode reacts with the hot carbon, burning it away
The anodes melt at the high temperatures used
The aluminium deposits on the anodes and blocks them
The cryolite dissolves the carbon anodes

questions.explanation: Oxygen gas is produced at the anode during aluminium extraction (2O²⁻ → O₂ + 4e⁻). At the high operating temperatures, this oxygen reacts with the carbon anodes: C + O₂ → CO₂. The anodes gradually burn away and must be replaced regularly, which adds to the cost of the process.
